cases.finding: DPBench directly exercises simultaneous shared-resource contention and coordination failure, but supplies the multi-agent organization, action protocol and communication structure itself. Published model/provider runs are not native canonical-harness S2 observations.

The native historical Magentic-One orchestrator ablation removes progress tracking, loop detection and explicit direction and changes end-task performance, but the benchmark tasks do not directly instantiate an S2 disturbance and the ablation spans both S2 and S3 mechanisms. Numeric results live only in the shared raw observation record.

MAFBench includes conflict-avoidance, matching, leader-election and consensus tasks, but its published topology implementation builds the coordination application itself and currently uses LangGraph as the runtime. Canonical LangGraph has S2=—, so these runs are not LangGraph.S2 evidence.

The benchmark varies coordination conditions over a common multi-agent coding substrate and includes concurrent-agent/conflict-resolution scenarios. It is a strong direct-S2 candidate, but the system-in-focus is multiple Claude agents plus a coordination condition and twining-mcp is not currently a canonical Index system.

cases.finding: Canonical Agent Teams exposes durable shared tasks/commitments and team coordination, but the public benchmark entry point currently directs users to the minimal jsonrpc-agent variant rather than the Agent Teams S2 path.
